key_insight: Adaptive shot allocation can reduce quantum debugging executions by focusing measurements on uncertain assertions while maintaining comparable debugging confidence.
engineering_relevance: Allocating shots across mid-circuit assertions offers a practical way to reduce measurement costs in statistical quantum program debugging.
method: Implement four allocation strategies in the CUDA-Q-based QDB debugger.
Compare equal split, static weight allocation, adaptive entropy routing, and sequential retirement.
Use repeated circuit execution and statistical hypothesis testing to check expected qubit-state characteristics.
evidence_signal: Evaluation across different circuits under noise-free and depolarizing-noise conditions reports substantially lower total shot usage with adaptive strategies, though the abstract provides no numerical results.
watch_item: Benefits under broader hardware noise models and larger circuits remain unestablished by the abstract.
paper_title: Shot Allocation Strategies in Debugging Quantum Circuits
